author: root/coordinator

checks.description: Disposable QEMU boots the SD/NFS-root source and writes the exact pinned full-image fixture to a distinct virtual eMMC target while proving the running source is outside the target and no host/physical block device is opened.

A complete flush and full readback match the exact source bytes/hash and expected GPT/partition layout; ambiguous, wrong, undersized, overlapping, missing, truncated, changed, failed or timed-out writes fail closed without a success record.

Tests and documentation preserve the offline-only evidence boundary and add one deduplicated future physical commissioning entry with prerequisites and stop conditions, without requesting the physical action now.

constraints.text: Use only disposable regular-file-backed QEMU media. Keep the guest network-root source independent of the virtual destination; verify the active root and image source cannot resolve to that destination. The host harness must refuse block-device paths, symlinks to block devices and paths outside its assigned disposable directory. State which SD/NFS Linux path QEMU reproduces and which H616 boot stages it does not model.

Pin source image length, SHA-256 and complete GPT layout. Test a full raw-image transfer including loader/GPT regions, flush and independent full-length readback. Compare bytes through the image boundary and validate both GPT headers and every expected partition boundary and identity. A changed source, short transfer, timeout or failed flush/readback must never produce a success record.

Do not accept a path, label, nominal capacity or serial alone as target identity. Bind QEMU target to the configured virtual disk and observed device identity; test substituted, ambiguous, undersized and source-overlap cases. QEMU checks are prototype evidence only; physical eMMC identification needs a separate reviewed adapter.

Bound fixture size, disk allocation, memory and test time. State the fixture geometry and retain the factory 8 GB image-footprint requirement; a small synthetic fixture or 32 GB virtual target does not establish release sizing.

Keep H12 queued as the single future physical commissioning task. Before use it needs an exact candidate image and target map, proof spare contents are expendable or exported, recovery plan, explicit authorization and independent high-consequence review immediately before write. Interruption or uncertainty must stop without automatic retry. This approval grants no physical write authority.

decision.rationale: Decision 0018 authorizes this bounded offline pilot. The H09/H10 records establish a supervised SD/NFS boot and read-only access to the installed spare eMMC; they do not establish write safety. The existing signed A/B updater changes only inactive OS slots, so a complete-image test addresses a distinct part of the owner's writerless goal. The bounded prototype therefore uses disposable QEMU media. Neither approval nor a passing QEMU test authorizes a printer write.

evidence.limitations: Test-only QEMU evidence. It does not emulate H616 Boot ROM/SPL/U-Boot, physical eMMC identification, physical write behavior, or printer boot. Five transient GFP_ATOMIC allocation warnings occurred during emulated network traffic, without observed dropped packets, TCP timeout, NFS error, panic or hash mismatch.
evidence.method: On Beelink, QEMU 8.2.2 booted the verified SD/NFS kernel/initramfs with read-only NFS root in a private network and mount namespace. It wrote a pinned synthetic 7,818,182,656-byte image to the one held-descriptor regular-file-backed 32,000,000,000-byte USB disk, checking exact guest path, serial, capacity and source separation. Guest and host did not open a host block device.

evidence.limitations: The 32 GB destination and image are synthetic; this does not authorize or validate physical eMMC writes. Failure injection tests are unit/native tests; QEMU success is the positive end-to-end write/readback path. The sparse image does not model worst-case allocation or flash wear.
evidence.method: The guest SHA-256 checked the entire source before write and during transfer, flushed the target, reopened and read the full image back; the full guest readback matched the source pin. The host independently read back the entire target extent and checked protective MBR, primary and backup GPT CRCs, disk GUID, and all six partition numbers, names, GUIDs, offsets and sizes. Ten focused tests cover changed/truncated source, GPT damage, target identity/size/path substitutions and ambiguity, source overlap, failed host readback, short I/O, timeout and flush refusal. Earlier QEMU attempts refused or stopped before any target write and produced no success receipt.

evidence.limitations: H12 remains queued and has not run. No real image was written and no printer, MCU, or physical block device was contacted.
evidence.method: The prototype is explicitly test-only and is not in the SD diagnostic image builder. Documentation records its invocation, synthetic source/target map, resource bounds, evidence hashes, failure boundaries, and a single queued H12 physical commissioning task with prerequisites and stop conditions.

tasks.title: Implement and verify a network-root full-image QEMU prototype

verification.rationale: Reviewed the complete five-file diff from e85e2f8 to clean HEAD b49173f, approved constraints, source hashes, and committed QEMU receipt. Reproduced all 10 focused tests, static ARM64 compilation, Python syntax, JSON parsing, Markdown link checks, and diff checks. The recorded run supports a complete synthetic-image write, guest flush/readback, independent host hash and GPT validation using disposable regular-file-backed QEMU media. The five transient guest allocation warnings did not coincide with a recorded transfer or integrity failure. This passes the offline prototype checks only; H616 boot stages, physical eMMC identity and writes, and printer boot remain unverified under H12.

title: Write and verify a full image to virtual eMMC from SD/NFS root
